# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 5, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 55 and nothing else, plus
the question the session asked it to settle: whether the path-comparison defect
three reviews had found three ways is closed as a class. It read the ticket, all
fifty-five records, the nineteen files of the focus set, `harness/journal.py`,
`harness/kpi.py`, `harness/tests/test_agents.py` and `CLAUDE.md`, and it
verified by running the module against planted records and against the real
journals of SEEN-105, SEEN-107, SEEN-108 and SEEN-109 rather than by reading it.

Verdict: **return**, on F1.

**On the class question.** Closed on the triage side, and checked by running it:
`normalise` on both sides, the prefix removed as a prefix, an absolute path
placed nowhere, a reference tail stripped whether it is a line, a hunk or a line
and a column, and `not excluded` told from `never seen` by the triage's own
files. Not closed on the route side, which is F1.

## The findings

**F1, high, `harness/calibration.py:363`.** The same class a fourth time, on the
route measure. `slice_rows` charges a finding only to a slice whose planned
files contain it, so a finding in a changed file that no slice named is charged
to nobody, and `verdict_routes` has nowhere to put what could not be charged.
Measured on planted journals: ten counted tickets, each with one downgraded and
one strongest slice and one blocking finding in a file no slice named, produce
downgraded rate 0.0 against strongest rate 0.0 and a printed go-live. Ten
blocking findings made a rate of exactly zero, and nothing in the routes section
said a finding had been dropped, where the triage section names everything it
could not place. A file changed but named by no slice is what the `slice_files`
check exists for, and it failed on this very ticket for three files.

**F2, medium, `harness/kpi.py:448`.** This ticket made a returning round record
its own findings, and `kpi.findings` still reads only the advance, so the weekly
report and the calibration report will state different findings for the same
ticket in the same commit with nothing saying why. Its docstring justifies
reading only the advance with an assumption this ticket's own second review
disproved.

**F3, low, `harness/calibration.py:199`.** The `and seen_by_triage` guard
restores the merge the fourth review removed whenever a triage record carries no
files list, and every `EscapeTest` fixture runs through that fallback rather than
through the real record shape, so the distinction the fourth review bought is
pinned by one test class only.

**F4, low, the ticket file.** `slice_files` fails on three files and the Outcome
accounts for two: `harness/doctor.py` is described in substance and named in
neither list, and the count of deviations is now wrong.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`red_before_green` verified line for line for all five attempts, each RED
matching the failure reason its advance states. `tests_added` passes but for F1
and F3. `acceptance_entries` passes, matched rather than counted. `slice_files`
settled as F4. `pull_request` unavailable. Ground rules checked by codepoint
rather than by eye; the only dashes in the branch are inside repowise's quoted
output in record 2.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded 13 of 19 files, 56.42 per cent. F1 lands in
`harness/calibration.py`, which the triage kept, so it is not an escape; F2 is
in `harness/kpi.py`, which is not in the diff's focus set at all and is a file
the triage never saw, which is the case its own fix is about. The round reads
clean, and the ticket is excluded from the window by name.
